propositions.text: The claimant is a citizen of Colombia claiming refugee protection under IRPA sections 96, 97(1)(a) and 97(1)(b).
propositions.quote: XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX is a citizen of Colombia. She claims for refugee protection pursuant to Sections 96, 97(1)(a) and 97(1)(b) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The claimant, a Colombian citizen, claims refugee protection under IRPA sections 96, 97(1)(a) and 97(1)(b).

propositions.text: She was actively involved in Colombian politics and had problems with FARC starting in 1987.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleges she was actively involved in Colombian politics. Her problems with the Fuerzas Armadas Revolucionaries de Colombia (FARC) guerrillas began in 1987

propositions.text: FARC demanded she help them, but she refused due to lack of authority.
propositions.quote: The FARC demanded that she XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX She told them that she had no authority to help them in that area.

propositions.text: In 1988, FARC demanded resignations; after killings, she stopped working as City Councillor in 1989.
propositions.quote: In 1988, the FARC demanded that XXXXX XXXXX, including her, resign from their positions. When the FARC began killing XXXXX XXXXX who failed to meet their demands, the claimant ended working as a City Councillor in 1989.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges political involvement and FARC threats starting 1987, leading to resignation in 1989.

propositions.text: In 1993, FARC confiscated her property; in 1995, she received threats to resign or die.
propositions.quote: In 1993, the FARC confiscated the claimant's XXXXX XXXXX with its contents. Subsequently, in 1995, when she became a XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX, she began receiving threatening letters from the FARC demanding that she resign from her position or die.

propositions.text: In 1997, her home was bombed and a colleague murdered by FARC; she resigned and moved to Bogota.
propositions.quote: In 1997, her home in XXXXX XXXXX was bombed and, six months later, her colleague, XXXXX XXXXX, was murdered by the FARC. As a result of her colleague's murder, she resigned from her position in the XXXXX XXXXX and permanently located in Bogota.

propositions.text: She maintained her position after relocating to Bogota.
propositions.quote: She maintained her XXXXX XXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges FARC confiscation, threats, bombing, colleague's murder, resignation, and relocation to Bogota.

propositions.text: In 1999, after a demilitarized zone agreement, she returned to her area.
propositions.quote: In 1999, after the Colombian government reached an agreement to create a demilitarized zone for the FARC, she returned to XXXXX XXXXX.

propositions.text: In 2001, she filed a denunciation against FARC for threats and extortion.
propositions.quote: In 2001, the claimant, accompanied with XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX, filed a denunciation against the FARC for continued threats and extortion demands.

propositions.text: In 2002, she filed a denunciation with Public Prosecutor for threats related to tenant backed by FARC.
propositions.quote: In XXXXX 2002, she filed a denunciation against the FARC with the Public Prosecutor's office in Bogota for threats made against her when her tenant, backed by the FARC, refused to vacate her house in XXXXX XXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges returning in 1999 and filing denunciations against FARC in 2001 and 2002.

propositions.text: The key issues are whether the claimant has subjective fear and if that fear is objectively well-founded.
propositions.quote: The determinative issues in this case are subjective and whether, at this time, her fear is objectively well-founded.

propositions.text: The panel finds claimant lacks subjective fear and her fear is not objectively well-founded.
propositions.quote: the panel does not find that the claimant has a subjective fear of persecution in Colombia, as well as her fear is not objectively well-founded.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant lacks subjective and objective fear of persecution.

propositions.text: Testimony under oath is presumed true unless valid reason to doubt it.
propositions.quote: testimony given under oath is presumed to be true, unless there is a valid reason to doubt its truthfulness.

propositions.text: Truth of witness story judged by harmony with probabilities a practical person would find reasonable.
propositions.quote: the real test of the truth of a story of a witness is that it be in harmony with the preponderance of probabilities which a practical and informed person would readily recognise as reasonable in that place and in those conditions.

propositions.text: Evidence is credible only if probably true, not just possibly true.
propositions.quote: the panel cannot be satisfied that, "the evidence is credible or trustworthy unless satisfied that it is probably so, not just possibly so".

paragraphs.summary: The court states rules on credibility: presumed truthful, judged by probabilities, must be probably true.

propositions.text: Panel considered all evidence and finds claimant lacks subjective fear and fear is not objectively well-founded.
propositions.quote: Based on the totality of the evidence adduced, the panel finds that the claimant lacked subjective fear which is not objectively well-founded.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant lacks subjective fear and objective basis after reviewing all evidence.

propositions.text: Claimant fears FARC; problems began 1987 but she left Colombia only in 2003.
propositions.quote: the claimant indicated that she fears the FARC guerrilla group in Colombia. She indicated that her problems with the FARC began in 1987 but she did not leave Colombia until 2003.

propositions.text: In 2002, she applied for refugee protection at Canadian Embassy in Bogota but was refused.
propositions.quote: She testified that in 2002 she applied for refugee protection at the Canadian Embassy in Bogota. When her application for refugee protection was refused, she decided to flee to Italy in XXXXX 2003.

propositions.text: She lived in Italy temporarily until 2007, then returned to Colombia despite fear.
propositions.quote: She lived in Italy on a temporary status until XXXXX 2007 and thereafter she decided to return to Colombia, the country where she feared persecution at the hands of the FARC.

propositions.text: She did not apply for asylum in Italy because she expected peace talks to succeed and return.
propositions.quote: She indicated that she did not apply for asylum in Italy because she intended to return to Colombia expecting the peace talks between the FARC and the Colombian Government to succeed.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant fears FARC but stayed in Italy until 2007 and returned to Colombia expecting peace talks to succeed.

propositions.text: Claimant's expectation to return after peace talks is unreasonable; talks collapsed in 2002 before she left.
propositions.quote: Her expectations to return to Colombia after peace talks between the Government of Colombia and the FARC succeeded are not reasonable since peace talks between the two parties had collapsed in XXXXX of 2002,4 before she left to go to Italy.

propositions.text: Long stay in Italy without asylum claim and return to Colombia indicate lack of subjective fear.
propositions.quote: The panel finds that the claimant's long stay in Italy, without making an attempt to file for asylum, and her return to Colombia is indicative of lack of subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's return to Colombia after peace talks collapsed and no asylum claim in Italy shows lack of subjective fear.

propositions.text: Six to seven months stay in Colombia before returning to Italy shows lack of subjective fear.
propositions.quote: Her six to seven months' stay in Colombia is indicative of lack of subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC.

propositions.text: Failure to claim asylum in Italy during second visit shows lack of subjective fear.
propositions.quote: Her failure to make an asylum claim during her second visit to Italy is another example of lack of subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC in Colombia.

propositions.text: Return to Colombia despite fear indicates lack of subjective fear.
propositions.quote: Her return to Colombia where she feared the FARC for the second time also indicates that she lacked subjective fear of persecution in that country.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's stays and asylum failures in Italy and returns to Colombia show lack of subjective fear.

propositions.text: Threats from FARC continued after return; she went to Mexico in 2008 and lived with daughter.
propositions.quote: After she returned to Colombia from Italy, threats from the FARC continued and as a result she decided to go to Mexico in XXXXX of 2008. In Mexico, she lived with her daughter until XXXXX, 2008 before returning to Colombia.

propositions.text: She did not file asylum in Mexico as she was only visiting her daughter.
propositions.quote: She indicated that she did not file for asylum in Mexico because she had no plans to do so since she was only visiting her daughter.

propositions.text: Failure to seek asylum in Mexico despite threats indicates lack of subjective fear.
propositions.quote: her failure to seek asylum in Mexico, a country signatory to refugee Convention, indicates that she lacked subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC in Colombia.

propositions.text: Returning to Colombia to get US visas is unreasonable; could have obtained them in Mexico.
propositions.quote: Her reason for returning to obtain USA visas from the USA embassy in Colombia is not reasonable since she could have obtained those visas at the USA embassy in Mexico.

propositions.text: Return to Colombia in 2008 shows lack of subjective fear.
propositions.quote: Her return to Colombia on XXXXX 2008 is another example of lack of subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC in Colombia.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges continued threats but court finds failure to seek asylum in Mexico and returns to Colombia show lack of subjective fear.

propositions.text: After getting US visas, she returned to Mexico in 2009 but did not regularize status, showing lack of subjective fear.
propositions.quote: After receiving the USA visas, she returned to Mexico in XXXXX 2009. Once again she made no attempt to regularize her status in Mexico. Her actions indicate her lack of subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC in Colombia.

propositions.text: She went from Mexico to Las Vegas then Canada, not planning asylum in USA to join brother in Canada.
propositions.quote: From Mexico she went to Las Vegas and then to Canada. She indicated that she did not plan to apply for asylum in the USA because she wanted to join her brother in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's failure to regularize status in Mexico and travel to Canada without US asylum plans shows lack of subjective fear.

propositions.text: Claimant's brother has been Canadian resident since 2003 and was a successful refugee applicant.
propositions.quote: The claimant's brother is a resident of Canada since 2003. He was a successful refugee applicant.

propositions.text: Claimant knew about Canadian refugee protection from 2002 embassy application.
propositions.quote: The claimant had knowledge about the refugee protection in Canada since she had applied for refugee protection at the Canadian embassy in Bogota in 2002.

propositions.text: Despite brother's status and contact, claimant did not try to regularize status in Canada earlier, choosing Italy and Mexico instead.
propositions.quote: Although her brother had status in Canada since 2003, and, given that she was in contact with him since he left Colombia, the claimant made no effort to come to Canada to regularize her status earlier. She chose to go to Italy and Mexico instead.

propositions.text: These actions indicate lack of subjective fear of persecution from FARC.
propositions.quote: Her actions indicate lack of subjective fear of persecution from the FARC in Colombia.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's failure to seek earlier Canadian status despite brother's presence shows lack of subjective fear.

propositions.text: Claimant's behavior and actions indicate lack of subjective fear of FARC persecution after 1997 resignation.
propositions.quote: Based on the evidence adduced, the claimant's behaviour and her actions indicate that she lacked subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC in Colombia. The panel is not persuaded to believe that she feared the FARC after she resigned from her XXXXX XXXXX position in 1997.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant lacked subjective fear of FARC persecution after 1997 resignation.

propositions.text: Claimant testified to continuous threats from FARC after resignation and personal contact by FARC commander.
propositions.quote: Moreover, the claimant testified that she was continuously threatened by the FARC, after she resigned from her position as a member of XXXXX XXXXX She also indicated that on one occasion she was personally contacted by the commander of the FARC from XXXXX XXXXX.

propositions.text: Claimant did not provide documentary evidence like police reports or affidavits to corroborate threats after 1997.
propositions.quote: At the hearing she did not provide any documentary evidence, such as a police report or an affidavit, to indicate that she was threatened by the FARC after her resignation from the XXXXX XXXXX in 1997.

propositions.text: No media articles or affidavits from daughter or colleagues to corroborate threats after resignation.
propositions.quote: She did not provide media articles and/or affidavits either from her daughter in Colombia or from other colleagues and friends to corroborate that she was threatened by the FARC after she left her XXXXX XXXXX position.

propositions.text: No persuasive reasons given for failure to provide such documents despite instruction to do so.
propositions.quote: Also she did not provide persuasive reasons for failing to provide such documents to help the panel in its decision. The onus is on her to establish her claim particularly when she was instructed in question 31 to provide documentary evidence to establish her claim.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges continued threats after resignation but court finds no documentary evidence or explanation for lack thereof.

propositions.text: Failure to provide documentary evidence raises serious doubt about FARC interest in harming claimant after resignation.
propositions.quote: Her failure to provide the aforementioned documentary evidence raises a serious doubt in the panel's mind as to whether the FARC had any further interest to harm the claimant when she resigned from the XXXXX XXXXX.

propositions.text: Panel does not believe claimant was threatened by FARC after resignation.
propositions.quote: The panel therefore does not believe that the claimant was threatened by the FARC after she resigned.

paragraphs.summary: The court doubts FARC interest in harming claimant after resignation due to lack of evidence and disbelieves post-resignation threats.

propositions.text: FARC demanded resignation which claimant complied with; panel not persuaded FARC had interest to harm her after.
propositions.quote: Also the FARC demanded that she resign from her position at the XXXXX XXXXX which she did. As a result, the panel is not persuaded to believe that the FARC had any interest to harm her after she complied with their demands.

propositions.text: Panel finds claimant fabricated story about threats after 1997 to bolster claim.
propositions.quote: The panel finds that the claimant has fabricated her story about threats from the FARC after 1997 to bolster her refugee claim.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant complied with FARC demands and fabricated post-1997 threats to bolster claim.

propositions.text: Panel does not believe FARC threatened claimant after 1997 resignation due to lack of interest.
propositions.quote: Based on the evidence adduced, the panel does not believe that the FARC threatened the claimant after she resigned from her position at the XXXXX XXXXX in 1997 because they had no interest to do so.

propositions.text: Panel finds claimant lacks objectively well-founded fear of persecution by FARC in Colombia.
propositions.quote: As a result, the panel does not find that the claimant has an objectively well-founded fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC in Colombia.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no FARC threat after resignation and no objectively well-founded fear of persecution.

propositions.text: Professor Hathaway says protracted postponement of refugee claim is relevant to evaluating sincerity of need for protection.
propositions.quote: Professor Hathaway has said that it is appropriate to inquire into the circumstances of any protracted postponement of a refugee claim as a means of evaluating the sincerity of the claimant's need for protection.

paragraphs.summary: Professor Hathaway states delay in refugee claim helps evaluate sincerity of protection need.

propositions.text: In Leon, waiting over five years to claim refugee status was found incredible by Justice Muldoon.
propositions.quote: In Leon, the claimant waited over five years to make a claim. Justice Muldoon of the Federal Court commented: It is incredible that he [the claimant] would believe that he could not make a refugee claim because he was an illegal ........ That is incredible. That he would wait for 5 years in that belief, if that belief were true, is even more incredible.

paragraphs.summary: In Leon, a five-year delay in refugee claim was found incredible by Federal Court Justice Muldoon.

propositions.text: Claimant lacked subjective fear of persecution by FARC and fear is not objectively well-founded
propositions.quote: because the claimant lacked subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC, and since her fear is not objectively well-founded

propositions.text: Less than a mere possibility that claimant would be persecuted by FARC if returned to Colombia
propositions.quote: there is less than a mere possibility that she would be persecuted by the FARC should she return to Colombia

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant lacks subjective and objective fear of persecution by FARC and that persecution is less than a mere possibility if returned to Colombia.

propositions.text: Panel's credibility findings apply to claimant's assertion of risk to life or cruel treatment in Colombia
propositions.quote: The panel's credibility findings also apply to the claimant's assertion that she faces a risk to his life or of being subjected to cruel and unusual treatment or punishment in Colombia

propositions.text: Claimant lacks subjective fear of persecution by FARC and fear is not objectively well-founded
propositions.quote: Since the claimant lacks subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC, and her fear is not objectively well-founded

propositions.text: Claimant does not face risk to life, cruel treatment, or torture if returned to Colombia
propositions.quote: the panel finds that the claimant does not face a risk to her life or to being subjected to cruel and unusual treatment or punishment or to a danger of being tortured, should she return to Colombia

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant's fear of risk to life or cruel treatment is not credible and not objectively well-founded, so no such risk exists if returned.

propositions.text: Review of all documentary evidence shows no persuasive evidence of risk other than general violence in Colombia
propositions.quote: Based on the documentary evidence, there is no persuasive evidence to indicate that, at this time, the claimant will be subjected to any other risk, other than the risk of general violence which all citizens in Colombia are subjected to

paragraphs.summary: The court finds documentary evidence shows no risk to claimant beyond general violence faced by all Colombian citizens.

propositions.text: Claimant is not a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection under IRPA sections 97(1)(a) and 97(1)(b)
propositions.quote: the panel finds that the claimant is not a Convention refugee, nor she is a person in need of protection pursuant to sections 97(1)(a) and 97(1)(b) of the IRPA

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor in need of protection under IRPA sections 97(1)(a) and (b).

propositions.text: Refugee Protection Division rejects claimant's refugee protection claim
propositions.quote: the Refugee Protection Division rejects the claim of XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX for refugee protection

paragraphs.summary: The court orders the Refugee Protection Division to reject the claimant's refugee protection claim.
